title: Keyframes: one still per live shot
judge_notes: File names are shot ids: keyframes/S03.png is shot S03 in screenplay.json. Each keyframe was made from the shot's character sheets, location plate and the previous approved keyframe, and is the first frame of its clip.

questions.text: Does every live shot have its keyframe file?
Is every keyframe in the screenplay's aspect?
Does every keyframe prompt carry its shot's bibles word for word?
Is every keyframe prompt free of requests to draw text, a logo or a number plate?
Did every keyframe pass its take checks within max_takes (none flagged)?
Does each keyframe show what its shot describes: framing, who is where, what each hand holds?
questions.evidence: Name each shot that differs and how.

questions.text: Does each character look like their sheet and bible in every keyframe (face, hair, fixed details)?
questions.evidence: Name any shot where a face drifts.

questions.text: Is the wardrobe the bible's in every keyframe?
questions.evidence: Name any shot with wrong clothes.

questions.text: Is the light the same time of day and from the same side across shots in the same place?
questions.evidence: Name any shot that breaks it.

questions.text: Are hands right (five fingers, a real grip) and phone screens turned away from the lens?
questions.evidence: Name any wrong hand or screen.

questions.text: Is every keyframe free of text, letters, logos, emblems, insignia and number plates?
questions.evidence: Quote nothing for a yes; for a no, name the file and where the text or mark is.

questions.text: Does each keyframe look like a real photograph (no plastic skin, no warped faces or objects)?
Does each keyframe leave room for its shot's action, with nobody cut off awkwardly at the frame edge?
Is screen direction kept between shots (who is frame-left and frame-right)?
